The vehicle involved in this case is a car bearing registration No. DL-1TA-0514,
which at the relevant time of accident was being driven by respondent no.1 (R1) Sh. Police Singh,
owned by respondent no. 2 (R2) Sh. Kailash Marik and insured with respondent no. 3 (R3) Royal Sundram General Insurance Co. Ltd.

When they reached in front of Hungary Embassy, Niti Marg,
Chanakyapuri, New Delhi, the offending car bearing registration No. DL-1TA-0514, which was being driven by respondent at a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner, hit the scooty from behind due to which they fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries.
Claimant was removed to Safdarjung Hospital, New Delhi, where his MLC was prepared.
3. Respondents no. 1 and 2 have filed their joint reply to the DAR wherein it is submitted that the respondent no. 1 was holding a valid and effective driving license which was valid upto 23.09.2017.
It is further submitted that the alleged offending vehicle was duly insured with respondent no. 3 w.e.f. 04.01.2017 to 03.01.2018.
It is submitted that the police officials in connivance with the claimant have falsely implicated them as well as the alleged offending vehicle in the present matter.
It is further submitted that the accident had taken place due to sole and absolute negligence on the part of deceased/rider of the scooty who was under the influence of alcohol.
4. Respondent no. 3/Insurance Company filed its legal offer for a sum of Rs.88,000/-, after deducting 15% amount towards contributory negligence, which was not accepted by the claimant.

5. It is pertinent to mention that the two connected DARs bearing Nos. D-973/17 qua the claimant and D-991/17 qua the deceased Sh. Sachin were filed on 30.10.2017 and since they both arise out of the same accident, they were consolidated for the purpose of trial vide Order dated 16.01.2018 and DAR No. 991/17 was directed to be treated as the lead case in which the evidence was to be recorded.

On the same day, the following consolidated issues were framed by this tribunal as:-

owned by respondent no. 2 and insured with respondent no. 3

1. Whether Sh. Sachin Kumar (deceased of DAR No. 991/17) sustained fatal injuries and Sh.
Chander Shekhar (injured of DAR No.973/17) sustained injuries in the accident which occurred on 09.06.2017 at about 1:20 AM, infront of Hungary Embassy, Niti Marg, Chanakyapuri, New Delhi caused by rash and negligent driving of vehicle No. DL-1TA-0514 being driven by respondent no.1,
owned by respondent no. 2 and insured with respondent no. 3 ? OPP.
10. Onus to prove this issue was upon the claimant.

The first question that needs to be decided is whether the accident was caused by the vehicle bearing registration No. DL-1TA-0514.
11.
In order to prove the same, the claimant has examined himself as PW2.

In his evidence by way of affidavit Ex. PW2/A, he narrated the manner of accident as follows :-
"That on unfortunate day of accident dated 09.06.2017 at around 01:00 A.M, when I as pillion rider along with my friend namely Sachin were going on scooty bearing No.
DL-3SDP-5895 to R.K. Puram via Tenjeeg Marg and reached in front of Hungary Embassy, Niti Marg, Chanakya Puri, New Delhi, One offending vehicle car bearing no. DL-1TA-0514 being driven by the respondent no.1 in rash, careless and negligent manner and at very high, fast and violent speed came and hit into the said vehicle from back side then due to this sudden and forceful impact, my friend and me fell down on the road and I sustained grievous, severe injuries on my left foot and ankle."
12. During cross examination, he deposed that neither he nor his friend Sachin had consumed alcohol at the time of accident.
Perusal of record reveals that Sh. Sachin was driving the scooty and the claimant was sitting as pillion rider.

Chargesheet including MLC of the injured (Ex.PW-2/2)
prove that the injured was a pillion rider.
The Insurance Company has not brought anything on record to show that it was the claimant who was driving the scooty.
Even though the MLC of claimant mentions "Alcohol intake +", however, his blood sample was not taken to ascertain whether or not alcohol limit in blood was within permissible limits.
Besides, the claimant was a pillion rider and contributory negligence cannot be imputed on him.
13. It is explicit from the testimony of PW2 that the occurrence of accident has not been disputed and the testimony of the witness in this regard has gone unrebutted.
Nothing material could be elicited from the cross examination of PW2 to disbelieve or discard his testimony.

It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a Civil Court and in Civil matters, the facts are required to be established on preponderance of probabilities and not beyond reasonable doubt, as are required in a criminal prosecution.
Reference in this regard is made to the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court reported as (2009) 13 SC 530 in Bimla Devi and others Vs.

21. ISSUE NO.2 2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, to what amount and from whom?
22.

As the issue No.1 has been proved in favour of the claimant, he has become entitled to be compensated for the injuries suffered by him in the accident, but the computation of compensation and liability to pay the same are required to be decided.
23. In terms of Section 168 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988, the compensation which is to be awarded by this Tribunal is required to be 'just'.
In injury cases, a claimant is entitled to two different kinds of compensation i.e. pecuniary as well as non- pecuniary damages.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343, has laid down heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases as:-
Pecuniary damages (Special Damages)
(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation,
nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure.
(ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising :
(a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment;
(b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability.

entities.text: Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (iii) Future medical expenses.
Non-pecuniary damages (General Damages)
(iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.
(v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage).

(vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity).
24.

Having considered the ratio of aforesaid judgment, the compensation payable to claimant is assessed hereinafter under the following heads as:-
(i) Medical or Treatment Expenses 25.

The claimant in his affidavit Ex. PW2/A has tendered on record his discharge summary as Ex.
PW2/3, as per which the claimant was admitted in Max Super Specialty Hospital, Saket on Chander Shekhar vs Police Singh on 8 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129201927/
5 09.06.2017 and was discharged on 17.06.2017 and was diagnosed with open grade IIIB fracture left both bone leg left + fracture Ist Metatarsal Left + Degloving Injury Left Foot + Heel Pad Avulsion Left and had undergone various operative procedures.

The claimant again admitted in the said hospital on 10.07.2017 and discharged on 12.07.2017.
26.
The claimant has also tendered on record her medical bills as Ex. PW2/6 (colly) which are totalling to a sum of Rs. 3,94,841/-.
The respondents have failed to lead any evidence to show that the said medical bills do not relate to the injuries suffered by the claimant in the aforesaid accident.
Thus, the testimony of PW-2 that he had spent the aforesaid amount towards medical expenses remained unrebutted and uncontroverted.
In the absence of any plausible evidence produced by respondents on record, there is no reason to disbelieve the testimony of PW-2 that he had spent the aforesaid amount towards medical expenses.
Hence, he is held entitled to Rs.3,94,841/- towards his medical expenses.
(ii) Loss of earnings 27.
The claimant in his affidavit Ex. PW2/A has claimed that he was doing job in MTS Company at New Delhi and was getting salary of Rs.15,000/- per month.
However, during cross examination, he deposed that he has not filed any income proof in order to substantiate his above claim.
He has tendered on record copies of his graduation certificate/marksheet and matriculation certificate as Ex. PW2/7 (colly).
However, perusal of these documents Ex. PW2/7 (colly) reveal that the claimant has studied upto 12th class.

28. Since the employment and income of the claimant has not been established on record, the minimum wages of matriculates is taken into account as per rates prevalent in Delhi which was Rs.16,962/- per month at the time of accident.
29. The claimant in his affidavit has claimed that he was bed ridden for around six months due to the injuries sustained in the accident.
Keeping in view the natures of injuries and duration of his treatment, this tribunal feels it just and reasonable to compensate him for loss of earning equivalent to a period of six months.
Therefore, under this head, he is being awarded an amount of Rs.1,01,772/- (Rs.16,962/- X 6 months).
(iii) Loss of future earnings 30.

As per disability certificate issued by Dr. RML Hospital, the claimant is the case of road traffic accident and had degloving injury left foot with metatarsal fracture, heel pad avulsion and fracture both bone LL Grade IVB.

The claimant was examined by the medical board and found to have a permanent disability score of 29%.
31.

The law with regard to grant of compensation due to permanent disability and determination of functional disability etc. was well settled by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Raj Kumar Vs.
Ajay Kumar & Anr., (2011) 1 SCC 343, wherein it has been held as under :-

sentences.text: The provision of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (`Act' for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident.
The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.

The court or tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable.
A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury.

This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned.

(See C. K. Subramonia Iyer vs. T. Kunhikuttan Nair - AIR 1970 SC 376, R. D.
Hattangadi vs. Pest Control (India) Ltd. - 1995 (1) SCC 551 and Baker vs. Willoughby - 1970 AC 467).
10. Ascertainment of the effect of the permanent disability on the actual earning capacity involves three steps.

sentences.text: The Tribunal has to first ascertain what activities the claimant could carry on in spite of the permanent disability and what he could not do as a result of the permanent ability (this is also relevant for awarding compensation under the head of loss of amenities of life).
The second step is to ascertain his avocation, profession and nature of work before the accident, as also his age.

The third step is to find out whether (i) the claimant is totally disabled from earning any kind of livelihood, or (ii) whether in spite of the permanent disability, the claimant could still effectively carry on the activities and functions, which he was earlier carrying on, or (iii) whether he was prevented or restricted from discharging his previous activities and functions, but could carry on some other or lesser scale of activities and functions so that he continues to earn or can continue to earn his livelihood.
For example, if the left hand of a claimant is amputated, the permanent physical or functional disablement may be assessed around 60%.
If the claimant was a driver or a carpenter, the actual loss of earning capacity may virtually be hundred percent, if he is neither able to drive or do carpentry.

On the other hand, if the claimant was a clerk in government service, the loss of his left hand may not result in loss of employment and he may still be continued as a clerk as he could perform his clerical functions; and in that event the loss of earning capacity will not be 100% as in the case of a driver or carpenter, nor 60% which is the actual physical disability, but far less.

In fact, there may not be any need to award any compensation under the head of `loss of future earnings', if the claimant continues in government service,
though he may be awarded compensation under the head of loss of amenities as a consequence of losing his hand.

Sometimes the injured claimant may be continued in service, but may not found suitable for discharging the duties attached to the post or job which he was earlier holding, on account of his disability, and may therefore be shifted to some other suitable but lesser post with lesser emoluments, in which case there should be a limited award under the head of loss of future earning capacity,
Chander Shekhar vs Police Singh on 8 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129201927/
7
taking note of the reduced earning capacity.

It may be noted that when compensation is awarded by treating the loss of future earning capacity as 100% (or even anything more than 50%), the need to award compensation separately under the head of loss of amenities or loss of expectation of life may disappear and as a result, only a token or nominal amount may have to be awarded under the head of loss of amenities or loss of expectation of life, as otherwise there may be a duplication in the award of compensation.
Be that as it may............."

32. Considering the legal position discussed above coupled with the testimony of PW2 and aforesaid discussions, the functional disability of claimant is, therefore, taken as 20% in relation to whole body.
33. To apply the multiplier, it is necessary to ascertain the age of the claimant.
The claimant has tendered on record copy of his Aadhaar card and PAN card as Ex. PW2/1 (colly) (OSR).
In Aadhaar card, the year of birth of claimant is found recorded as 1990 whereas in PAN card of claimant, his date of birth is mentioned as 07.09.1990.
Hence, going by these documents, the age of claimant comes out to be around 26 years, 9 months and 2 days at the time of accident.
Therefore, in view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma & Ors. Vs.

Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr., (2009) 6 SCC 121, which has also been upheld by the Constitution Bench of the Hon'ble Apex Court in a judgment of National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors., SLP (Civil) No. 25590 of 2014 dated 31.10.2017

34. Further, the claimant is also held entitled to 40% future prospects in view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Pranay Sethi & Ors.(Supra).
Thus, the loss of future earnings caused to the claimant due to his permanent disability comes to Rs.9,68,869/- (rounded off) (Rs.16,962/- X 12 X 20/100 X 17 X 140/100).
(iv) Mental and Physical Shock, Pain and Sufferings & Loss of Amenities 35.
As stated above, the claimant had suffered grievous injuries and permanent disability in the accident.

Though, it is not possible to exactly compensate him for the shock, pain and sufferings etc.
which he had actually suffered because of the above injuries, but an effort has to be made to compensate him for the same in a just and reasonable manner.

Hence, keeping in view the extent and nature of the injuries suffered by the claimant and duration of the treatment taken by him etc.,
an amount of Rs.70,000/- each is being awarded to him towards (i) mental and physical shock and (ii) for pain and sufferings respectively.
Further, an amount of Rs.30,000/- is also awarded to him towards the loss of amenities suffered by him during said period of his treatment.
Thus, he is awarded total amount of Rs.1,70,000/- under this head.
(v) Conveyance, Special Diet and Attendant Charges 36.
The claimant in his affidavit has claimed that he had spent an amount of Rs.20,000/- on conveyance, Rs.30,000/- towards special diet and Rs. 20,000/- towards attendant charges.

Still this Tribunal can very well take note of the requirement of conveyance for claimant for frequently visiting the hospitals and doctors in connection with his treatment and special diet for his early recovery from the injuries suffered because of the accident.
Considering the facts and circumstances of the present case, an amount of Rs.15,000/- is being awarded to the claimant towards conveyance and Rs.20,000/- towards special diet.

37. Keeping in view the nature of injuries and disability suffered by the claimant, he would have required assistance of some family member/attendant for doing his daily routine work for atleast six months, therefore, a sum of Rs.10,000/- per month for six months is also being awarded to the claimant towards attendant charges.

The claimant is thus entitled to an amount of Rs.95,000/-
(Rs.15,000/- + Rs. 20,000/- + Rs. 10,000/- X 6 months) under this head.
(vi) Loss of prospects of marriage 38.

Keeping in view the nature and extent of disability, an inference can also be drawn that the marriage prospects of the claimant will certainly be affected to great extent and he will have difficulties in finding a suitable match and hence, an amount of Rs.1,00,000/- is also awarded to the claimant under this head.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Chargesheet including MLC of the injured (Ex.PW-2/2)
prove that the injured was a pillion rider.
The Insurance Company has not brought anything on record to show that it was the claimant who was driving the scooty.
Even though the MLC of claimant mentions "Alcohol intake +", however, his blood sample was not taken to ascertain whether or not alcohol limit in blood was within permissible limits.
Besides, the claimant was a pillion rider and contributory negligence cannot be imputed on him.
13. It is explicit from the testimony of PW2 that the occurrence of accident has not been disputed and the testimony of the witness in this regard has gone unrebutted.
Nothing material could be elicited from the cross examination of PW2 to disbelieve or discard his testimony.
In cases National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pushpa Rana, 2009 ACJ 287 and United India Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Deepak Goel and Ors., 2014 (2) TAC 846 (Del.) decided by the Coordinate Bench of the Hon'ble Delhi High Court, it was held that "......where the claimants filed either the certified copies of the criminal record or the criminal record showing the completion of investigation by police or issuance of charge sheet under Section 279/304A IPC or the certified copy of FIR or the recovery of the mechanical inspection report of the offending vehicle, then these documents are sufficient proof to reach to a conclusion that the driver was negligent particularly when there is no defence available from the side of driver."
16. Reliance is being placed upon the judgment of Hon'ble Delhi High Court in case Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Meera Devi & ors., 2021 LawSuit (Del) 2021 wherein it was held that "......in view of Delhi Motor Accident Claim Tribunal Rules, 2008, contents of DAR has to be presumed to be correct and read in evidence without formal proof of the same unless proof to the contrary was produced."
17. The Hon'ble Apex Court in Mangla Ram Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. & Ors., 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303 has observed that filing of charge sheet against the driver prima facie points towards his complicity in driving the vehicle rashly and negligently.
18. It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a Civil Court and in Civil matters, the facts are required to be established on preponderance of probabilities and not beyond reasonable doubt, as are required in a criminal prosecution.
Reference in this regard is made to the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court reported as (2009) 13 SC 530 in Bimla Devi and others Vs.
Road Transport Corporation and others
19. Pertinently, respondent no. 1 himself was the best witness who could have stepped into the witness box to rebut his involvement in the aforesaid accident, which he has failed to do.
Therefore,
an adverse inference is drawn against the respondent no.1/driver in terms of judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi passed in the case of Cholamandalam M.S. General Insurance Company Ltd. Vs.
Kamlesh, reported in 2009 (3) AD (Delhi) 310.
20.
In view of foregoing discussion, it stands proved on preponderance of probability that the aforesaid accident took place due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle bearing registration no. DL-1TA-0514 and the said vehicle at that time was driven by respondent no. 1,

23. In terms of Section 168 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988, the compensation which is to be awarded by this Tribunal is required to be 'just'.
In injury cases, a claimant is entitled to two different kinds of compensation i.e. pecuniary as well as non- pecuniary damages.
The law with regard to grant of compensation due to permanent disability and determination of functional disability etc. was well settled by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Raj Kumar Vs.
Ajay Kumar & Anr., (2011) 1 SCC 343, wherein it has been held as under :-
Chander Shekhar vs Police Singh on 8 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129201927/
6 "4.
The provision of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (`Act' for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident.
A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury.
This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned.
(See C. K. Subramonia Iyer vs. T. Kunhikuttan Nair - AIR 1970 SC 376, R. D.
Hattangadi vs. Pest Control (India) Ltd. - 1995 (1) SCC 551 and Baker vs. Willoughby - 1970 AC 467).
10. Ascertainment of the effect of the permanent disability on the actual earning capacity involves three steps.
In Aadhaar card, the year of birth of claimant is found recorded as 1990 whereas in PAN card of claimant, his date of birth is mentioned as 07.09.1990.
Hence, going by these documents, the age of claimant comes out to be around 26 years, 9 months and 2 days at the time of accident.
Therefore, in view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma & Ors. Vs.
Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr., (2009) 6 SCC 121, which has also been upheld by the Constitution Bench of the Hon'ble Apex Court in a judgment of National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors., SLP (Civil) No. 25590 of 2014 dated 31.10.2017
, the multiplier of '17' is applicable for calculating the loss of future earnings of the claimant arising out of above disability.
Hence, keeping in view the extent and nature of the injuries suffered by the claimant and duration of the treatment taken by him etc.,
an amount of Rs.70,000/- each is being awarded to him towards (i) mental and physical shock and (ii) for pain and sufferings respectively.
However, he has not placed on record any document in order to substantiate the above claims.
Considering the facts and circumstances of the present case, an amount of Rs.15,000/- is being awarded to the claimant towards conveyance and Rs.20,000/- towards special diet.
